Field.name: RootName
Field.usage: Root name of data set (omit a or b for dual-axis set)

Field.name: StackExtension
Field.usage: Extension of raw stack excluding period (optional)
Field.manpage: Extension of raw stack excluding the period. If this is not specified, the program will assume the extension ".st" unless the \fB-style\fR option is entered. With a \fB-style\fR option and no specified stack extension, it will look for ".st", ".mrc", ".hdf", ".tif", and ".tiff" and require that only one of those types is present. With this entry, which could in principle be arbitrary, it will not care if files with other extensions are present.

Field.name: DualAxis
Field.usage: Dual-axis data set

Field.name: MontagedImages
Field.usage: Data are montaged

Field.name: BackupDirectory
Field.usage: Directory for backing up small files
Field.manpage: Directory for backing up small files. Commands to save such files are placed in a script named "savework", which is run at end of every command file. The directory need not exist yet.

Field.name: PixelSize
Field.usage: Pixel size of images in nanometers (required)
Field.manpage: Pixel size of images in nanometers. This entry is required.

Field.name: GoldBeadSize
Field.usage: Size of gold beads in nanometers (required)
Field.manpage: Size of gold beads in nanometers. This entry is required. Enter 0 if you are not going to track fiducials.

Field.name: RotationAngle
Field.usage: Angle from the vertical to the tilt axis in raw images (required)
Field.manpage: Angle from the vertical to the tilt axis in raw images for the A axis or only axis. This entry is required.

Field.name: BRotationAngle
Field.usage: Angle from the vertical to the tilt axis for B axis
Field.manpage: Angle from the vertical to the tilt axis for B axis. The default for a dual-axis set is the angle entered for A.

Field.name: FirstAndIncAngle
Field.usage: First tilt angle and tilt angle increment
Field.manpage: First tilt angle and tilt angle increment for the A axis or only axis.

Field.name: BFirstAndIncAngle
Field.usage: First tilt angle and tilt angle increment for B axis

Field.name: UseRawtltFile
Field.usage: Take tilt angle from a .rawtlt file for A or only axis
Field.manpage: Take tilt angle from a .rawtlt file for the A axis or only axis.

Field.name: BUseRawtltFile
Field.usage: Take tilt angle from a .rawtlt file for B axis

Field.name: ExtractAngles
Field.usage: Extract tilt angles from data file for A or only axis
Field.manpage: Extract tilt angles from data file for the A axis or only axis if the file does not already exist. This entry implies -userawtlt.

Field.name: BExtractAngles
Field.usage: Extract tilt angles from data file for B axis

Field.name: TiltAngles
Field.usage: Complete list of tilt angles, on one line with no spaces
Field.manpage: Complete list of tilt angles for the A or only axis, on one line with no spaces.

Field.name: BTiltAngles
Field.usage: Complete list of tilt angles for the B axis

Field.name: TwoDirectionsAngle
Field.usage: Tilt series was bi-directional from given starting angle
Field.manpage: The tilt series was taken in two directions starting at the given angle. The first half of the series will be defined as a separate view group for Tiltalign(1) and Beadtrack(1), from the first view through the first occurrence of the given angle.

Field.name: BTwoDirectionsAngle
Field.usage: Tilt series for B axis was bi-directional from given starting angle

Field.name: ReversedBidirectional
Field.usage: First acquired part of tilt series is second part of stack
Field.manpage: The part of the tilt series acquired first is the second part of the tilt series stack. Without this option, the program assumes that the tilt series is in the same order as the file produced by automated acquisition software, in which the part acquired first is inverted in order and placed in the beginning of the stack.

Field.name: BReversedBidirectional
Field.usage: First acquired part of B axis tilt series is second part of stack

Field.name: DoseSymmetricAngle
Field.usage: Tilt series was dose-symmetric from given starting angle
Field.manpage: The tilt series was taken with a dose-symmetric scheme, starting at the given angle. This angle is assumed to correspond to zero tilt of the specimen itself, so with this option, the negative of this angle will be set as an angle offset in xcorr.com, track.com, and align.com.

Field.name: BDoseSymmetricAngle
Field.usage: Tilt series for B axis was dose-symmetric from given starting angle
Field.manpage: The tilt series for the B axis was taken with a dose-symmetric scheme, starting at the given angle.

Field.name: ViewsToSkip
Field.usage: List of views to exclude from processing for A or only axis
Field.manpage: List of views to exclude from processing for A or only axis. This entry and the next are fed into view exclusion lists in track*.com, align*.com, and tilt*.com.

Field.name: BViewsToSkip
Field.usage: List of views to exclude from processing for B axis

Field.name: DistortionField
Field.usage: Correct image distortion with the given .idf file
Field.manpage: Correct image distortion with the given .idf file. The file will be copied to the current directory.

Field.name: BinningOfImages
Field.usage: Binning of raw images (needed to undistort if ambiguous)
Field.manpage: Binning of the raw images; this entry is needed for distortion correction unless there is no ambiguity about whether they are binned; i.e., unless the images are not binned and are too large to be considered binned.

Field.name: GradientTable
Field.usage: Correct for magnification gradients using the given .mgt file
Field.manpage: Correct for magnification gradients using the given .mgt file. Extractmagrad(1) will be run to extract mag gradient files for each axis.

Field.name: FocusWasAdjusted
Field.usage: Focus was adjusted between frames when acquiring montage
Field.manpage: Focus was adjusted between frames when acquiring montage for the A axis or the only axis

Field.name: BFocusWasAdjusted
Field.usage: Focus was adjusted between montage frames for the B axis

Field.name: VoltageInKV
Field.usage: Microscope voltage in kV

Field.name: SphericalAberration
Field.usage: Spherical aberration

Field.name: NoiseConfigFile
Field.usage: Configuration file listing noise files for ctfplotter

Field.name: Defocus
Field.usage: Defocus in nanometers, with underfocus positive

Field.name: CopyCTFfiles
Field.usage: Just copy files for CTF plotting and correction (1: plotting, 2: correction, 3: both)
Field.manpage: Just copy files for CTF plotting and correction (1 for plotting, 2 for correction, 3 for both)

Field.name: SetFEIPixelSize
Field.usage: Set standard pixel spacing in image file(s) from FEI software
Field.manpage: Set the standard pixel spacing in the header of each image file if it comes from FEI software. The pixel size from the extended header will be multiplied by the binning of the images, if any, and placed in the standard header location, so that it will propagate through the processing. If there is already a standard pixel spacing not equal to 1, 2, 3, or 4, it will not be modified.

autodoc.Field:
change FNM Name of file with directives for changing parameters
'Name of file with directives for changing parameters. A directive <has the form "comparam.comfile.process.option>value" where "comparam" is a required prefix for directives to be processed by Copytomocoms, "comfile" is the root name of the command file with optional "a" or "b", "process" is the name of a program being run on a line starting with "$", "option" is an option to add or modify, and "value" is its value. An example is <"comparam.xcorra.tiltxcorr.FilterSigma1">0.02". Files are processed in order, and a duplicate entry for an option generally overrides an earlier one. However, for a dual-axis data set, a directive specific to a particular axis, such as that example, will always be preferred over a generic directive with no "a" or "b" on the command file name. For a single-axis data set, directives with a "b" are ignored and ones with an "a" or with no "a" or "b" are treated equivalently, such that later ones override earlier ones.</"comparam.xcorra.tiltxcorr.FilterSigma1>

Field.name: OneParameterChange
Field.usage: One directive for changing parameters
Field.manpage: One directive for changing parameters, in the format just described. Entries with this option are processed after, and can override, ones entered from files, and later ones override earlier ones.

Field.name: NamingStyle
Field.usage: 0, 1 or 2 for descriptive, mrc, or hdf extensions on image file names
Field.manpage: 0 for output image files to have descriptive extensions like ".preali", 1 for extension ".mrc", or 2 for extension ".hdf". In the latter two cases the usual descriptive text is put before the extension, and command files will contain an environment variable setting to make programs generate files of the corresponding type.

Field.name: HalfFloatModeOutput
Field.usage: 2 to output files as 16-bit floats, 1 to do so only if float input
Field.manpage: 2 to set the mode for output files to half-floats (16-bit floats) unconditionally, or 1 to do so only when the input file is floating point. Half-floats are useful for producing smaller files when the input stack is floating point, and may also be useful if a wide range of values need to be represented. The range of 16-bit floats is -65504 to 65504; values are stored with 11-bit precision down to 6.1e-5 and 10-bit precision down to 6.0e-8. This option currently governs the aligned stack, outputs from CTF correction and 2-D filtering, and reconstruction. The output from gold erasing will also be affected if this option is entered through a template.

Field.name: MakeComExtensionPcm
Field.usage: 0 or 1 to name output command files with extension ".com" or ".pcm"
Field.manpage: 0 or 1 to name output command files with extension ".com" or ".pcm". The latter is not yet supported by Etomo.

Field.name: XImageSize
Field.usage: X size of image data (needed if data file not present)

Field.name: YImageSize
Field.usage: Y size of image data (needed if data file not present)

Field.name: usage
Field.usage: Print help output
